title: Automatic Generation of Vectorizing Compilers for Customizable Digital Signal Processors
problem: Building auto-vectorizing compilers for DSP architectures is a large, error-prone investment that must be repeated for each new DSP or ISA customization. Engineers must handwrite many customized kernels to achieve vectorized execution on diverse DSP platforms.
motivation: Embedded applications require vectorized execution on DSPs to achieve optimal power-performance trade-offs, making automated compiler generation critical for reducing development time and engineering effort.
method: Isaria uses equality saturation to search for vectorized DSP code by automatically synthesizing sound rewrite rules from ISA specifications without manual hand-crafting. The framework discovers phase structure within rules to improve compilation performance and schedules rule application at compile time while pruning intermediate search states, enabling rapid generation of high-quality vectorizing compilers.
key_novelty: Automatic synthesis of correct-by-construction vectorization rewrite rules directly from ISA specifications, enabling compiler generation without manual expert effort.
contributions: Isaria framework for automatically generating vectorizing compilers from ISA specifications
Automatic synthesis of sound rewrite rules from ISA definitions eliminating manual rule crafting
Phase structure discovery and compile-time scheduling to optimize compilation performance
Demonstration achieving up to 6.9x speedup over existing DSP libraries while remaining competitive with expert-built compilers

metrics.speedup: up to 6.9x over existing DSP libraries, competitive with expert-built compilers
